claim.quote: Here we report measurements of the fine structure in the n = 2 states of antihydrogen, the antimatter counterpart of the hydrogen atom.

key_value_text.quote: The resulting value is consistent with the predictions of quantum electrodynamics to a precision of 2 per cent.
key_value_text.value: Fine-structure splitting consistent with QED to a precision of 2 per cent

name: Investigation of the fine structure of antihydrogen

significance.quote: The resulting value is consistent with the predictions of quantum electrodynamics to a precision of 2 per cent.
significance.value: Consistent with QED predictions to 2 per cent (fine structure) and 11 per cent (Lamb shift)

summary.plain: ALPHA measured the fine structure of antihydrogen with lasers. The result agrees with quantum electrodynamics to a precision of 2 per cent, and the classic Lamb shift agrees with theory at the 11 per cent level.
summary.technical: Optical excitation of the 1S–2P Lyman-alpha transitions at 1 T to 16 ppb; the inferred zero-field 2P1/2–2P3/2 splitting is consistent with QED to 2 per cent, and, with the earlier 1S–2S value, the Lamb shift is consistent with theory at 11 per cent.

title: Investigation of the fine structure of antihydrogen
why_it_matters: The abstract calls the result an important step towards precision tests of charge–parity–time symmetry and towards the antiproton charge radius.
